destination.title: Long-range SYK dynamics and protected boundary operator data
destination.question: How do long-range disorder correlations affect spectra, chaos and spatial scrambling in the specified solvable SYK-like fixed points, and what operator data can be protected in the related boundary Yukawa-SYK construction by its free higher-dimensional bulk?
destination.summary: A composite question preserving the source's two constructions: two-dimensional long-range dynamics and three-dimensional boundary operator data coupled to a four-dimensional free bulk. Their dimensions, observables and protection mechanisms remain distinct.

systems: Two-dimensional long-range bosonic SYK-like fixed points
Three-dimensional boundary Yukawa-SYK coupled to a four-dimensional free bulk
targets: Dependence of the long-range model's spectrum on disorder correlations
Chaos and spatial scrambling in the long-range model
Operator data protected by the free bulk in the boundary construction
regimes: The source-specified solvable long-range fixed-point family
The separate boundary/free-bulk construction and its stated protection regime
assumptions: The two constructions are related source components, not one identical physical system.
Free-bulk protection is investigated in the boundary construction and is not transferred to the long-range model.
Solvability does not itself establish universal maximal chaos or a common gravitational dual.
conventions: Two-dimensional long-range dynamics is distinguished from three-dimensional boundary data and its four-dimensional bulk.
Spatial scrambling and operator protection are separate observables and mechanisms.
includes: The complete compound question linking long-range dynamical calculations with the related boundary operator-data construction
Separate assessment of spectral, chaos, scrambling and protection claims within their stated systems
excludes: A universal protection theorem across SYK-like models
Identification of free-bulk protection with a common reparametrization or chaos mechanism
A shared gravitational holographic interpretation inferred solely from SYK terminology
Splitting the original source into new atomic source units

methods: Analysis of disorder-correlation dependence of spectra and scrambling
Boundary constraints associated with a free higher-dimensional bulk

sources.title: Long range SYK model and boundary SYK model

evidence.text: Solve large-N Schwinger–Dyson equations with an infrared power-law propagator after dropping the free inverse propagator. Extract exchanged dimensions from ladder-kernel eigenvalues satisfying k(Δ,ℓ)=1; the boundary theory first has a coupled matrix kernel.

sources.title: Long range SYK model and boundary SYK model

evidence.text: Expand four-point functions in conformal partial waves, use shadow symmetry and a Sommerfeld–Watson-like complex-spin contour deformation, then analytically continue to the OTOC second sheet. Compare momentum saddle contributions with pole residues in Regge and light-cone limits.

sources.title: Long range SYK model and boundary SYK model

evidence.text: Construct the free bulk propagator by images and Fourier transform parallel to the boundary. Boundary central-charge data are extracted from stress-tensor OPE residues; hyperbolic chaos follows from the Regge intercept.

membershipSample.placementReason: The proposed composite question covers both long-range SYK spectra and scrambling and protected boundary Yukawa-SYK operator data, with their dimensions and mechanisms kept distinct.
membershipSample.placementQualification: n0 preserves the full compound question. q29 covers long-range spectra, chaos and spatial scrambling but limits its boundary construction to a chaos observable; q3 covers conformal data and free-bulk protection without the spatial-scrambling program. Neither is independently complete. The supplied regions do not establish a suitable whole home solely from SYK or bulk–boundary terminology. Retaining the supported composite n0 avoids a union while preserving separate dimensions and protection mechanisms.
